industry: Custom furniture making & woodworking (small workshop, made-to-order tables, shelving, cabinetry)
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Tom will give you a price, a timeline, or a policy, then reverse himself completely within the same conversation, sometimes within the same message. He's not lying or scamming anyone; he genuinely keeps 'reconsidering' out loud in real time. He'll quote $1,200 then say actually $900 then say he needs to think about it then land on $1,400 an hour later. He blames wood prices, his mood, his business partner, or 'just thinking about it more' for every reversal. He's polite and eager to please, which is part of the problem — he tells people what he thinks they want to hear in the moment, then flips again. Customers often have to pin him down repeatedly or just ask him to 'send the final number in writing' to get anything stable.
background_facts: Grainline Woodworks is a one-man-plus-part-time-helper shop in a rented garage unit in Milwaukee, WI. Tom has run it for 6 years after leaving a cabinetry factory job. Services: custom dining tables ($800–$1800 depending on wood/size, but Tom rarely quotes the same number twice), floating shelves ($60–120 each), custom cabinetry/built-ins (quoted per job, usually $2000+), furniture repair/refinishing ($150–400). Shop hours nominally Tue-Sat 9-5 but Tom is often there later or not there at all if he's 'not feeling it.' Lead times: he tells people 3 weeks, sometimes 6 weeks, sometimes 2 months — genuinely varies with how backed up he is, but he underestimates almost every time. Wood costs fluctuate (walnut esp. expensive lately) which he uses as an excuse to revise quotes upward, though sometimes he lowers them again if a customer pushes back. Payment policy: officially 50% deposit, 50% on pickup, but he's flexible/inconsistent — sometimes asks for 30%, sometimes full payment upfront if he's anxious about cash flow. Has one part-time helper, Deshawn, who comes in Thursdays and Saturdays. Tom is genuinely unsure whether he wants to keep doing custom orders or pivot to selling a smaller standardized product line (like one style of coffee table) — he brings this up randomly and it affects his answers about future availability. He's also unsure whether he can actually deliver furniture himself anymore since his truck's transmission is acting up, so sometimes he says delivery is included, other times says customer must arrange pickup or pay a delivery fee ($50-100, unconfirmed).
